findings.title: Team admins who are not owners are denied access
findings.body: This permission check requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. Those are distinct roles, so an admin who is not also an owner fails this check and is denied even though the error path is intended to permit team admins or owners. Use an OR between the role checks so either role grants access.

findings.title: Guest deduplication is case-sensitive
findings.body: Email addresses are compared as exact strings here, so a request can add an existing attendee again using different casing (for example, `Guest@example.com` versus `guest@example.com`). This can create duplicate attendee records and send duplicate invitations; normalize addresses consistently for validation, blacklist checks, and existing-attendee comparisons.

findings.title: Calendar updates use the caller's credentials
findings.body: The caller may be an attendee rather than the organizer, but the EventManager is initialized with `ctx.user` and that user's credentials. Adding guests can therefore attempt to update the attendee's calendar instead of the booking owner's calendar, or fail when the attendee has no suitable calendar integration. Use credentials belonging to the calendar owner for this update.

findings.title: Existing attendees can receive a new-booking invitation
findings.body: This chooses the scheduled-booking email by checking the submitted guest list, not the guests actually inserted. If the request includes an address that already belongs to the booking alongside a new address, the existing attendee matches `newGuests` and receives another scheduled invitation instead of the guest-added update email. Pass the filtered, newly inserted addresses to this function.
